title: Will Russia officially announce a new mobilisation of reservists by 31 October 2026?
criteria: YES if between 10 and 31 Oct 2026 (Moscow time) a presidential decree or an official announcement by the Russian president or government declares a mobilisation (partial or general) of reservists, as published on kremlin.ru / pravo.gov.ru or reported by two major wire services. Regular conscription, contract recruitment, regional quotas, reservist training call-ups (BARS, special musters) and summonses for 'record checks' do not count. Otherwise NO.
reason: Pre-mortem (it is 31 Oct and I was wrong): a sudden front collapse or a decision already taken behind closed doors; neither story has visible evidence now. Opening: no battlefield shock of the 2022 Kharkiv kind; the index is elevated but the substitutes are working.

title: Will Russia legally bar reservists as a category from leaving the country by 30 June 2027?
criteria: YES if by 30 Jun 2027 a Russian federal law, presidential decree or government decree enters into force that restricts departure abroad for men in the military reserve as a category (for example all reservists of certain ages or ranks), without an individual summons or call-up order having been served. Restrictions that apply only to men already served a summons, to conscripts, or to specific professions with state secrets do not count. Source: pravo.gov.ru text plus two major outlets. Otherwise NO.
reason: Opening: the legal machinery for individual restrictions exists; a category-wide ban is a political step not yet visible.

title: Will the presidential decree expanding Russian military police search powers be signed by 30 November 2026?

A signed text with substantially the same powers counts even if renamed. Still a draft, withdrawn or merged into a law: NO.
reason: Opening: draft published 8 Oct (RBC, MK, Izvestia); signing speed is the open question.

title: Will Russia and Ukraine reach a full ceasefire that takes effect by 31 December 2026?
criteria: YES if a formal agreement between Russia and Ukraine to halt hostilities along the entire front line is announced by both governments and takes effect between 10 Oct and 31 Dec 2026. Partial truces (energy-only, sea-only, holiday truces, prisoner-exchange pauses) do not count. Source: official statements of both governments, or two major wire services. Otherwise NO.
reason: Opening: talks about talks, no sign either side accepts a freeze on the current line.

title: Will Russia publicly commit to a reciprocal halt of strikes on energy infrastructure by 20 November 2026?
criteria: YES if between 10 Oct and 20 Nov 2026 the Kremlin, Russia's president or its foreign ministry publicly states that Russia will stop (or has stopped) striking Ukraine's energy infrastructure as part of a reciprocal arrangement with Ukraine, as reported by two major wire services. Statements by third parties (for example the US president) that both sides agreed do not count without Russia's own confirmation. Otherwise NO.
reason: Opening: an offer is on the table but both sides are escalating against each other's infrastructure this week.

title: Will another data centre in Russia be damaged by a drone or missile strike between 10 October and 15 November 2026?

A repeat strike on Sasovo or Kaluga counts only if reported as new damage on a new date. Debris falling nearby without damage to the facility does not count. Otherwise NO.

title: Will any NATO member formally request Article 4 consultations between 10 October and 31 December 2026?

reason: Opening: flank incidents are frequent, but 2026 incidents have not been taken to Article 4.
